title: Activation Funnel Dashboard Spec (Lifecycle Growth Sprint) — Draft Requirements
content:
Context / why this exists
We’re running the 4-week Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint (email onboarding v2, console nudges, retargeting). We need a single, trusted dashboard that:
1) Measures the activation funnel end-to-end with consistent event definitions (so experiment readouts aren’t arguing about instrumentation).
2) Enables segmented diagnosis (email vs console vs organic, experiment variants vs holdout, region, SDK, etc.).
3) Alerts on sudden regressions after launches (e.g., duplicate events fix, nudge rollout, email vendor changes, throttling).

Audience
- Primary: Growth + Product owners (Ben Carter, Marissa Cole) and Eng partners who ship/monitor.
- Secondary: Support/Sales (sanity checks when activation dips correlate with spikes in tickets or lead handoffs).

Non-goals
- This is not a full retention/monetization suite. We’ll include D7/D30 “early retention” as supporting panels, but the core view is activation within 7 days.
- Not rebuilding the entire event taxonomy doc here; we reference ENG-10492 / PR #28431 for canonical definitions.

Dashboard name + location
- Name: “Hosted API — Activation Funnel (Lifecycle Growth)”
- Location: Observability Pack → Product Analytics → Growth
- Access: Company-wide read; edit rights to Observability owners + Analytics platform lead.

Data sources and freshness
- Source events: product analytics stream (server-side where possible). Canonical events from PR redwood#28431.
- Attribution fields: marketing attribution table (UTMs) + email send logs (where permitted by policy).
- Experiment cohorts: feature-flag assignment / holdout assignment from PR redwood#28477.
- Data freshness target: < 2 hours for top-line funnel; < 6 hours for segmented breakdowns (acceptable during sprint).
- Backfill: we should backfill last 28 days (or as available) once dedupe fix from PR redwood#28521 is deployed.

Key definitions (executive summary)
Primary activation outcomes (within 7 days of signup):
A1. First successful request (first inference call returns 2xx / non-error)
A2. First 100k tokens (cumulative generated + prompt tokens metered reaches 100,000)
Supporting metrics:
- TTFT (Time to First Token): p50/p90 from first request start → first token streamed/received
- Time-to-first-successful-request (signup → A1)
- D7 active usage: any successful request between day 7 and day 8 from signup (or defined window)

Funnel stages (required)
The dashboard must represent the canonical funnel for Hosted API self-serve:
Stage 0: Signup created
Stage 1: API key created
Stage 2: First request attempted
Stage 3: First successful request (A1)
Stage 4: First 100k tokens (A2)

Notes:
- Stages 2 and 3 must be distinct to detect errors/SDK friction (attempted vs succeeded).
- A2 should use metering source of truth (token counters) rather than client-side events.

Event mapping (canonical names + required properties)
Use the canonical event names and properties as implemented in PR redwood#28431 (and dedupe/bugfix behavior in PR redwood#28521). The dashboard logic should rely on:
- user_id (stable) and workspace_id/org_id (stable)
- event_time (server-side timestamp preferred)
- distinct_id/session_id (for debugging only; not primary counting)
- region (request region / console region)
- sdk (typescript/python/none) and sdk_version if available
- model_family or model_id (optional for later diagnostics)
- error_code/error_type for failed requests
- experiment flags: lifecycle_email_v2_variant, console_nudges_variant, holdout_group

Counting rules
- Primary reporting unit: “new signup” cohort (user_id) per day.
- Funnel conversions are based on unique users reaching each stage at least once within the window.
- Windowing:
  - Default view: signup cohort day, measured over 7 days after signup.
  - Secondary view: rolling 7-day cohort.
- Dedupe:
  - If signup is emitted multiple times, use earliest signup timestamp per user_id (PR redwood#28521 is expected to reduce duplicates, but dashboard must still guard).
- Cross-device:
  - If API key created in console and first request happens elsewhere, user_id linkage must be consistent.

Dashboard layout (required panels)
Panel group 1 — Top-line funnel (must be above the fold)
1) Funnel visualization: Stage 0→1→2→3→4 with counts + conversion rates
- Default filter: last 14 signup cohorts
- Toggle: counts vs rates
- Tooltip: stage definitions + counting window

2) Activation KPI scorecard (single row)
- Activation to A1 within 7 days (primary)
- Activation to A2 within 7 days (primary)
- Median time-to-A1 (supporting)
- TTFT p50 / p90 (supporting)

Panel group 2 — Trend + experiment impact
3) Time series: A1 activation rate by signup cohort day
- Show: overall + by experiment arm (email v2 A/B, console nudges A/B, holdout)
- Annotate: launch dates for experiment changes (manually maintained annotation list during sprint)

4) Time series: A2 (100k tokens) activation rate by signup cohort day
- Same segmentation as above

5) Decomposition: step drop-offs
- A set of bar charts or small multiples showing biggest drop-offs by stage:
  - Signup→API key
  - API key→First attempt
  - Attempt→Success
  - Success→100k tokens
- Each shows top contributing segment(s) when drop increases.

Panel group 3 — Quality & performance diagnostics
6) First request success rate (attempt→success)
- Trend + by error_type/error_code
- Use to catch bad SDK releases, auth changes, or rate limit misconfig.

7) TTFT distribution (p50/p90) for first successful request
- By region and by model_family (optional), and by streaming enabled flag if available.

8) Time to first request (signup→first attempt) distribution
- By entry path/source (docs/quickstart, console only, email click-through)

Panel group 4 — Breakdown dimensions (required filters)
Global dashboard filters:
- Date range (signup cohort days)
- Region (us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-south, etc.)
- Acquisition/source:
  - utm_source/utm_campaign (if present)
  - “email_onboarding” click-through (if available)
  - “console_nudge_cta” (if available)
- Experiment:
  - lifecycle_email_v2_variant (A/B)
  - console_nudges_variant (A/B)
  - holdout_group (true/false)
- SDK (python/typescript/rest/unknown)
- Customer type proxy (self-serve vs sales-assisted) — if we have a reliable flag; otherwise omit from default and keep as optional.

Panel group 5 — Guardrails / operational health
9) Volume sanity: signups per day + event ingestion health
- Shows raw signups, raw events ingested for key events, and % missing required properties
- Purpose: detect instrumentation regressions or pipeline gaps (see INT-3310 precedent)

10) Support correlation (optional for sprint)
- A small panel that overlays count of onboarding-related support tickets (e.g., “not receiving onboarding email”, “API key issues”) if easily available.

Alerting (required)
We need alerts that are actionable and minimize noise. Proposed alerts:

A) Activation regression alert (A1)
Trigger when:
- A1 activation rate for the last 24 hours of signup cohorts drops by >= 20% relative to the trailing 7-day baseline (same weekday adjustment if available), AND
- Minimum volume: >= 200 signups in the evaluated window, AND
- Drop persists for at least 2 consecutive data refreshes (to avoid partial ingestion blips).
Routing:
- On-call analytics/observability channel + Growth owner.
Suggested channel: #eng-platform or #marketing (confirm).

B) Funnel step-specific regression (Signup→API key OR Attempt→Success)
Trigger when:
- Any single step conversion rate drops by >= 25% vs trailing 7-day baseline, min volume >= 200 signups.
Notes:
- Attempt→Success regression is higher severity (likely product/SDK breakage).

C) Instrumentation health alert (missing properties / event volume)
Trigger when:
- Event count for a key stage (api_key_created OR request_attempted OR request_succeeded) falls by >= 30% vs baseline while signups are stable (within +/- 10%), OR
- % of events missing required properties (user_id, workspace_id, region) exceeds 2%.

D) TTFT performance regression
Trigger when:
- TTFT p90 for first successful request increases by >= 30% vs trailing 7-day baseline in any major region (min N >= 100 first successes).

Alert annotations / “known changes”
During the sprint we will have multiple deployments. We should maintain a short list of known change events to annotate:
- Email v2 ramp changes / throttling changes
- Console nudge experiment flip
- Dedupe fix deployment (PR #28521)
- Feature flag schema changes

Interpretation and gotchas
- Activation rates can move due to cohort mix changes (campaigns, bot signups, partner traffic). We should monitor signup quality signals (e.g., email domain buckets, suspicious traffic) if available.
- After dedupe fixes, historical comparisons may shift. Prefer comparing post-fix windows or apply dedupe in the dashboard logic.
- Retargeting impact: retargeting may influence “activation” indirectly; attribution will be imperfect. We should avoid over-segmenting the top-line funnel and keep retargeting breakdowns as secondary.

Implementation notes (to unblock ENG-10533)
- Build on the panels from PR observability-pack#241 and expand to include the alert thresholds and experiment segmentations above.
- Confirm canonical tables/views:
  - analytics.events_* (raw)
  - analytics.activation_funnel_daily (materialized view recommended)
  - analytics.experiment_assignments (from feature flags)
- Ensure dashboards use the same activation window logic as PM-651 KPI definitions.

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Counting unit: user_id vs workspace_id. Default recommendation: user_id for funnel (more direct “developer activation”), but add a toggle for workspace_id to support enterprise/pro team behavior.
2) Define “first request attempted”: include only inference endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings) or any API call? Recommendation: inference only.
3) TTFT measurement: do we have server-side streaming timestamps for “first token”? If not, we may approximate using client telemetry; document limitations.
4) Holdout enforcement: ensure holdout_group is stable and available in the analytics dataset (PR #28477). If absent, we can only do pre/post comparisons.

Appendix — Proposed default views for sprint readouts
- Default dashboard link (top-line): Overall A1/A2 + funnel for last 14 signup cohorts
- Experiment view: A1/A2 by email variant + console nudge variant + holdout
- Debug view: Attempt→Success by error_code + SDK version

Change log
- 2026-01-12: Initial draft created (Allison)
- 2026-01-20: Added experiment segmentation requirements + alert thresholds (Sergio/Ben)
- 2026-01-31: Updated for dedupe fix notes (PR #28521) and data freshness expectations (Mei/Logan)
- 2026-02-04: Clarified step definitions (attempt vs success) and added instrumentation health alert criteria
